description:
Captured 2026-08-04 from a half-formed idea the maintainer deferred -- CONFIRM THE INTENT before building.

As stated: 'I want boundary layers to be implemented for the pipe... should have inlet and outlet'.

Context it came out of: we had just run examples/mesh_studio (outram-blender, --features foam-mesh) on a cylinder primitive (r=2.0 m, h=10.5 m), which produced 34210 cells via the cfmesh tet -> dual -> prism-layer pipeline and exported an OpenFOAM polyMesh.

Likely reading (UNVERIFIED -- ask first): a pipe/cylinder meshed for CFD needs its boundary split into named patches -- inlet and outlet on the two end caps, wall on the curved surface -- and prism/boundary layers should be grown on the WALL only, not on the inlet/outlet planes. Growing layers on an inlet/outlet face is a classic meshing error. Today the boundary-layer controls in Mesh Studio (prism layers / first thickness / expansion ratio) appear to apply without any per-patch distinction, and it is not established whether the exported polyMesh names its patches at all.

Worth checking as part of this:
- Does outram-park-fork-cfmesh's pipeline expose per-patch boundary-layer control?
- Does the polyMesh writer emit meaningful patch names/types (patch vs wall) or one lumped boundary?
- Mesh quality on the cylinder run was already marginal (max non-orthogonality 87.2 deg, max skewness 7.994, and a stage note 'Delaunay improvement skipped -- no valid improving flips on this geometry'). Restricting layers to the wall may improve this.

Related: op-hzs.34 (outram-blender wall boundary-layer / prism-layer insertion).
title: Mesh Studio / cfmesh: pipe geometry with named inlet + outlet patches and wall boundary layers

acceptance_criteria: WGSL and Rust root-buffer capacities agree; a cubic that reports 4 critical points cannot index out of bounds on either side; regression test covers the clustered-triple-root cubic above.
description:
Found independently by two agents auditing the GPU surface-distance kernel, 2026-08-06. Latent, NOT the cause of op-9s8.11, but a genuine CPU/GPU divergence waiting for a degenerate cubic.

CAPACITY MISMATCH: the Roots struct in WGSL holds array<f32,4> and push_unique caps at "out.n < 4u" (wgsl:35, :77). The Rust mirror declares "let mut crit = [0.0f32; 3]" (surface_distance.rs:458) and push_unique_f32 caps at out.len() = 3. So the WGSL side can report FOUR critical points where Rust can only report three.

A cubic cannot HAVE 4 real roots, but collect_real_roots can REPORT 4: up to 3 bracketed roots plus critical points passing the residual test, when f32 noise splits a clustered triple root by more than push_unique's dedup radius of 1.0e-5 * (1.0 + abs(r)).

REPRODUCED by random search (400k trials):
  cubic_real_roots(1.0, -2.30112, 1.19506, -0.179715) returns n = 4
    -> [0.33104599, 0.33115199, 0.33128500, 1.63881624]
    true roots: 0.331034, 0.331270, 1.638816
  The three cluster members are ~1e-4 apart, wider than the 1.33e-5 dedup radius.

CONSEQUENCE when crit3.n == 4 (wgsl:227-228 passes ncr=4 alongside a 3-element crits array):
  - wgsl:141-143 and :150-152 read crits[3] -- out of bounds on array<f32,3>
  - wgsl:147-153 build bp with nb = 1 + 4 + 1 = 6, so bp[5] is an out-of-bounds WRITE on array<f32,5>, and the loop at wgsl:157 then reads bp[5]

WGSL bounds-CLAMPS rather than trapping, so this corrupts silently: the final breakpoint becomes crits[3] instead of +m, one interval collapses to zero width, and roots beyond the last critical point are MISSED -- wrong distance or INF returned with no diagnostic.

The Rust mirror cannot hit this: its capacity-3 cap makes the state unreachable. That asymmetry is the bug.

FIX DIRECTION: make the capacities agree. Either size the WGSL crits array to 4 and bp to 6, or cap push_unique at 3 on the cubic path so WGSL matches Rust. Whichever is chosen, apply it to BOTH sides -- the two are supposed to be twins.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-06, in the same pass as op-9s8.11 (same two files, same class of defect: WGSL and the Rust mirror drifting apart).

Both sides now clamp the cubic's root count to the mathematical maximum:
  const MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS = 3
  WGSL cubic_real_roots: out.n = min(out.n, MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS) before returning
  Rust cubic_real_roots_f32: .min(MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS) on the returned count

That is what keeps quartic_real_roots' 3-element crits array and collect_real_roots' 5-element bp array in bounds: with ncr <= 3, nb reaches at most 1 + 3 + 1 = 5, so bp[5] is never written and crits[3] is never read.

On the Rust side the caller's 3-slot buffer already bounded the count, so the clamp is normally a no-op there -- it is stated explicitly so the invariant is enforced the same way on both sides, rather than resting on a buffer size on one side and nothing at all on the other. That asymmetry was the bug.

Verified: full crate suite 197 passed, 0 failed; cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android clean.

NOT directly regression-tested: the trigger needs a cubic whose clustered triple root splits by more than push_unique's dedup radius (the reproducer found by random search was cubic_real_roots(1.0, -2.30112, 1.19506, -0.179715) -> n = 4). A targeted unit test for that input would be worth adding; filing that thought here rather than claiming coverage we do not have.

title: WGSL/Rust capacity mismatch: crits[3] OOB read and bp[5] OOB write when the derivative cubic reports 4 roots

description:
crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/mod.rs lists `kta` -- KTA packed-bed pressure drop (friction side of the bed)` under 'Planned (tracked in beads, not yet present)'.

That is now stale. The KTA correlation landed 2026-08-11 under op-jyyp.12 as crates/tampines/src/gas_phase/kta_bed.rs, verified against the VTB gold values (friction factor 1.983395 vs published 1.983, +0.0199 %; gradient 3493.167 Pa/m vs published 3493, +0.0048 %; drop 34.93167 kPa vs 34.93).

Placement rationale, recorded in gas_phase/mod.rs and gas_phase/kta_bed.rs module docs: KTA is a gas-side FRICTION closure that needs gas_phase::properties (helium EOS + transport) and shares the low-Mach framing with gas_phase::pipe, whereas pebble_bed is the CONDUCTION stack (ZBS, and the planned triso/pebble/cht layers).

Maintainer decision needed -- either:
  (a) accept the split and just update pebble_bed/mod.rs's planned list to point at gas_phase::kta_bed, or
  (b) move kta_bed.rs under pebble_bed/ and have it depend on gas_phase::properties.

The gas_phase agent did not edit pebble_bed/mod.rs (owned by other agents in the same session), so the note is still there. Also check whether op-jyyp.2 ('HTR-10: Ergun / KTA packed-bed pressure drop -- implement the existing todo!()') is now satisfied by gas_phase/kta_bed.rs, or whether it refers to a different todo!() site.
title: tampines pebble_bed/mod.rs: stale 'kta planned here' note -- KTA landed under gas_phase/ instead

notes.content: SN (discrete-ordinates) solver ported. Files under neutronics/sn/: quadrature.rs (level-symmetric S2/S4/S6, weights renorm to 4pi), sweep.rs (scattering-source inner iteration + per-direction upwind streaming/collision solve via fvm::div+sp+su, Gauss-Seidel), eigenvalue.rs (k-eigenvalue power iteration), mod.rs (SnNeutronics: scaffold new() + real with_cross_sections(); reuses DiffusionXsFields::materialize; Sigma_t=removal+self-scatter). Isotropic P0 scattering; anisotropic Legendre moments deferred (matches diffusion port). V&V (2026-07-15, all pass): k_inf no-scatter 3.0 to 4e-16; k_inf self-scatter to 4e-7; SN->diffusion limit 45.6 pcm (<1%); S2->S4->S6 monotone angular convergence; quadrature moment checks (sum w=4pi, 2nd moment 4pi/3). 6/6 SN tests + 33/33 neutronics tests pass (incl. un-editable mod.rs scaffold tests). clippy clean, Android check ok. Verified in isolated worktree at HEAD (sibling broke main-tree build via multi_region/mesh_region.rs h_vol field). NOT committed.
